name: Treaty with the Menominee, 1848 (Treaty of Lake Poygan)
promises: Article 2: the Menominee ceded all their lands in Wisconsin.

Article 3: the United States gave them, 'for a home, to be held as Indians' lands are held', land west of the Mississippi ceded by the Chippewa and Pillager bands in 1847, guaranteed to contain not less than 600,000 acres.
Article 4: a further $350,000, paid at the times and for the purposes set out in the treaty.
today: The Menominee did not move to the Minnesota land; the Treaty of Wolf River of May 12, 1854 (10 Stat. 1064) gave it back to the United States and set apart a reservation on the Wolf River in Wisconsin. The 1954 Termination Act applied to that 1854 reservation, not to land this treaty created. No Indian Claims Commission decision and no Court of Claims opinion on this treaty was found.

nationVoice.summary: The Tribe publishes the full text of the 1848 treaty among its historical documents.

openQuestions: The Court of Claims opinion of 1941 (95 Ct. Cl. 232) concerns the 1854 reservation's swamp lands; none of the later Menominee opinions opened concerns the 1848 price or the Minnesota land.
treaties.json lists Royce area 321 (Minnesota) with this treaty; that is the 600,000-acre western tract given, not land ceded by the Menominee. The cession is area 271.
A deeper pass could look for a Menominee claim about the 1848 consideration under the 1935 jurisdictional act and for a Menominee account of Oshkosh's refusal to move to Crow Wing.

Audit 2026-11-08: dates, 9 Stat. 952, the Article 3 quote and the 600,000-acre guarantee checked against the OSU text; Article 4 amount added. The Wolf River treaty citation (10 Stat. 1064, May 12, 1854) checked. No Menominee Court of Claims opinion in the Caselaw Access Project concerns this treaty.

plain.promised: For all their Wisconsin land, the Menominee were to get money and a western home of at least 600,000 acres in Minnesota.
plain.happened: The Menominee did not move; an 1854 treaty traded the Minnesota land for a Wolf River reservation in Wisconsin. No ruling on this treaty was found.
plain.today: The Menominee publish the treaty text. No claim about its price was found.
